title: Matrix — authority, approvals and escalation
content:
Matrix used by Theo, the Practice Team Leader, and every department and its AI agents, to decide what the team can action and what needs a human decision. AI agents gather facts, draft, check, calculate, compare and recommend; people approve everything below. Only Amelia, Caldova's Senior Risk Adviser, gives advice.

Human approval ALWAYS required — decision and approver:
1 Every Statement of Advice and Record of Advice — Amelia signs.
2 Replacing or cancelling any existing cover — the client decides with Amelia; the SoA sets out the replacement disclosures.
3 Accepting a loading, an exclusion or a decline at underwriting — the client decides with Amelia.
4 Lodging any claim, and every death or terminal illness claim — Theo approves through the Teams approval card before Ben lodges.
5 Blocking a request on financial-crime grounds, and referring suspected fraud to an insurer — Theo.
6 Any change to policy ownership, beneficiaries or bank details — Theo, after Financial Crime has confirmed the request on the client's verified contact details.
7 Advice with total cover of $2,000,000 or more on one case — Theo's second review.
8 Complaint responses — Theo.
9 Any communication to a fraud victim, a seriously ill client or a bereaved family — a person approves it before it goes: Cara for her letters, and Theo for every message to a bereaved family.

Escalate to Financial Crime: every new client (KYC); any change to contact or bank details within 30 days before a claim or payment; documents that may be altered; a payment account in another name; a PEP or sanctions match; anything that doesn't fit the file, such as activity during a travel notice.

Escalate to the Team Leader at once: vulnerable clients (serious illness, injury, financial stress, bereavement, scams, age or cognitive decline); any complaint, or any mention of AFCA or legal action; an insurer that misses a Life Code timeframe or its own service standard; any request the agents can't complete; every high-risk financial crime rating.

Caldova service standards: requests acknowledged, and anything not in good order explained, within 1 business day; applications lodged within 2 business days of the Authority to Proceed; approved claims lodged the same or next business day; clients and families updated at least every 10 business days while anything is open; vulnerable clients have one named contact.

Insurer timeframes to track (Life Insurance Code of Practice, CALI 2025 edition — binds insurers, not Caldova): decision on income-related claims within 2 months of the Claim Received Date or the end of the waiting period, if later (cl 5.48); lump-sum claims (death, terminal illness, trauma, TPD) within 6 months (cl 5.49); written decision within 15 business days of receiving all information (cl 5.50); progress updates at least every 20 business days (cl 5.6).

Complaints (ASIC RG 271): final written response within 30 calendar days for standard complaints, which include complaints about how an insurance claim is handled (RG 271.32(d)); a complaint about a declined claim or the value of a claim needs a written response even if it is resolved within 5 business days (RG 271.75). Every response tells the client they can take the complaint to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA) if they aren't satisfied.

Records: best-interests steps, the advice and why it is appropriate — 7 years (ASIC Instrument 2024/508); Records of Advice — 7 years (Corporations Regulations reg 7.7.09(3)); commission consent records — at least 5 years (Corporations Act s1101C(3)).

Quality: Theo audits every advice case with total cover of $2,000,000 or more, every claim and every financial-crime block, plus a sample of other files each month, against the best-interests safe-harbour steps (s961B(2)) and 'Guide — in-good-order checklist for advice and claims'.
